article.title: Why the Average Customer May Not Be a Real Customer
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Companies often describe the “average customer.” They may say the average customer spends $80 per visit, buys five times a year, or is 42 years old. These numbers are useful summaries, but the person they describe may not actually exist. Imagine a store with two groups. One group spends about $20 per visit, while another spends about $140. The average may be $80, even though very few customers spend close to that amount. The distribution has two different patterns, and the mean hides them. Skewed data creates another problem. A small number of very high spenders can pull the average upward. In that case, the median may describe a typical customer better. The same issue appears with purchase frequency, income, account balance, and many other customer metrics. This does not mean averages are bad. The mean is useful for totals and financial planning because total value divided by the number of customers has a clear meaning. But it should not automatically become a customer persona. Analysts should look at the distribution, median, percentiles, and important segments before saying what a typical customer does. They should also ask whether the population contains very different groups, such as new and long-term customers. A good report might say, “Average annual spend is $960, but the median is $420 and the top ten percent account for a large share of sales.” That sentence gives more context than the average alone. An average is a summary of data, not necessarily a description of a real person. Analysts should state the population, observation window, assumptions, and decision point before interpreting the result. A useful review separates the observed pattern from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. This discipline makes the analysis easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate to stakeholders.
paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文重點是不要讓單一摘要數字、留下來的樣本、模型選擇結果或統計調整取代對資料生成機制的理解。分析時要先界定母體、時間點、selection mechanism 與真正要回答的 business question，再判斷觀察到的差異可以支持到什麼程度。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：単一の要約値、生き残ったsample、modelによるselection、統計的な調整だけでdata generating processを置き換えて考えないことが重要である。母集団、時点、selection mechanism、business questionを先に定義し、観察された差がどこまでの結論を支持できるかを判断する。
